summary: Three related path-confinement defects across esm.sh's request/storage/web-serving trust boundaries let untrusted input (an HTTP header, a tarball entry name, and a raw URL request path) reach filesystem write/read operations without being confined to its intended base directory, enabling arbitrary file write and/or read outside the intended root in each case.

findings.area: server/router.go POST /transform and GET /+<hash>.<ext> handlers, server/build_resolver.go normalizeSavePath
findings.trust_boundary: Untrusted, unauthenticated HTTP request header (X-Zone-Id) incorporated into an on-disk storage key
findings.root_cause: normalizeSavePath prepends the caller-supplied X-Zone-Id header value directly to the storage key with no validation; fsStorage.Put/Get then resolve that key via filepath.Join(fs.root, key), which lets a sufficient run of '../' segments in the header escape fs.root.
findings.security_impact: Arbitrary file write (via POST /transform) and arbitrary file read (via GET /+<hash>.<ext>) outside the configured storage root, reachable by any unauthenticated client that can set an HTTP header (CWE-22), potentially escalating to remote code execution or persistence if the written file is later loaded or executed.
findings.behavior_before_fix: An X-Zone-Id header containing path-traversal segments is accepted and used to construct the storage key without validation, allowing the resulting file write/read to land outside the intended storage root.
findings.remediation: X-Zone-Id is now validated as a syntactically valid domain (valid.IsDomain) at both the write and read call sites and discarded (treated as absent) when invalid, before it can reach normalizeSavePath.
findings.behavior_after_fix: A path-traversal or otherwise non-domain X-Zone-Id value is ignored; the request proceeds as if no X-Zone-Id header were sent, and no file is written or read outside the storage root.

findings.trust_boundary: Untrusted tar entry names inside a package tarball fetched from a configured npm registry
findings.root_cause: Entry names are normalized with path.Clean after stripping only the tarball's first path segment; path.Clean does not confine a relative path to a base directory, so a crafted entry name with enough '../' segments still escapes the package's extraction directory when joined via path.Join.
findings.security_impact: Arbitrary file write outside the package install directory during normal package installation/build (CWE-22), reachable via any tarball the server ever fetches and extracts.
findings.behavior_before_fix: A tarball entry name containing path-traversal segments extracts to a location outside the intended node_modules/<pkg> directory.
findings.remediation: Entry names are now normalized with utils.NormalizePathname (absolute-rooted, so leading '../' segments collapse at the root instead of escaping) before the first-segment strip and join.
findings.behavior_after_fix: A crafted traversal entry name resolves to a path inside the package directory (or is otherwise confined); no file is written outside it.

findings.area: web/handler.go Handler.ServeHTTP default route (root module's serve/dev commands, a separate built program from server/esmd), web/utils.go validateModule
findings.trust_boundary: The raw, attacker-controlled HTTP request URL path
findings.root_cause: The default (non-special-cased) route joins the raw request path directly into the configured app directory via filepath.Join with no traversal or NUL-byte validation before Lstat/serving the file. web/utils.go additionally required an unrelated one-line compile-compatibility fix (a logger.Source struct field renamed by the pinned esbuild-internal dependency) so this program compiles at all; that change carries no security impact of its own.
findings.security_impact: Arbitrary file read outside the configured application directory, reachable by any unauthenticated HTTP client against the root module's own serve/dev commands (CWE-22).
findings.behavior_before_fix: A request path containing traversal segments (or an embedded NUL byte) resolves to, and serves, a file outside the app directory.
findings.remediation: The request path is validated (filepath.IsLocal after stripping the leading slash, plus a NUL-byte check) before being joined into the app directory; invalid paths are rejected with 400.
findings.behavior_after_fix: A crafted traversal or NUL-containing request path is rejected with 400 instead of reaching the filesystem; legitimate requests for existing in-app-directory files are served unchanged.

preserved_legitimate_behaviors: Requests with no X-Zone-Id header continue to build/cache/retrieve transforms under the unzoned (root) storage prefix.
Requests with a syntactically valid domain X-Zone-Id continue to be stored/retrieved under that zone's own prefix.
POST /transform and GET /+<hash>.<ext> response shapes and status codes for well-formed requests are unchanged.
Well-formed package tarballs, including nested legitimate paths, continue to extract to their expected locations.
Requests for files that genuinely exist inside the configured app directory continue to be served exactly as before.
